note: Small lean up: Getinge's Q3 shows the ~30M tariff refund probably lands against a 193 bar, but it is a one-off and the last refund-aided beat was sold; organic momentum offsets Getinge's softer demand and the margin pressure.

Mild negative: IDC's -20% PC units after the pull-forward, a larger NOK FX drag and a habit of missing EPS outweigh TD SYNNEX's steady European billings; moves on the outlook tone are large and observed.

Negative: ICA outgrew the market, so Willys likely grew below it, and Willys price investment costs margin, after a +19% re-rating on buy upgrades in a name whose last four report days fell 7-15%; the 3.9% short is not crowded.
Near zero: the AHRI US shipment rebound is mostly in the +3.5-4% organic bar, and it roughly offsets the record of small misses punished hard and a tough cash-flow comparison.
Non-result: the bar is disputed, and WISAG's 29.9999% floor inference offsets the pre-announced Danish arbitration charge's headline risk; thin name, so the size is still real.

Slight negative: three sell-side upgrades and +24% over 60 days raise the bar on a name that sold its last confirmations; Danaher's bioprocess read is mostly priced and below SSB's own pace; no Q3 consensus was sourced.

Near zero: swap-rate yield pressure on valuations is partly offset by the Bridge being bought below its underlying value and by insider buying; the property-management decline is already in the earnings capacity; release at 14:00 in session.
Slight negative: the earning-capacity arithmetic gives in line to marginally light against a one-analyst 1.10 bar, and Swedish property peers were sold on their Q3 prints the day before.

Positive on a thin, volatile, one-analyst name: a structural gross-margin gain of 1.5-2.5pp against an adjusted 41.6% base with no published profit bar, Clas Ohlson's strong Aug/Sep and board buying late in the quarter; the cost base and a weak y/y cash comparison offset part of it.

Lean up: the discount to a NAV rebuilt from public prices has widened to ~16-17% from 5-10% while the buyback paused, and on the last two report days the official NAV pulled the price toward it; buyback restart optional upside.

Slight negative: Q3 runs on the July earnings capacity against a 176 bar that leaves no room, the company habitually lands a few percent under, and LTV prints higher after debt-funded deals; the earnings-capacity step-up is priced.
Near zero: the NRG Pizza vacancy dents the earnings-capacity path but is mostly priced, against an issuer buyback near half of daily volume and an optional Kungens kurva lease signing.

Balanced: Worldpanel points to Q2 grocery growth above the broker bar, but the October panel implies a soft start to H2; the guide narrowing is mostly priced in the +8% Tesco run-up; the 6.7% building short is fuel either way.
Lean down: SEB's own pre-close NII/NFI steers sit below the FactSet bar while peers are being sold on NII misses this season; the capital-return hit is mostly priced after the -4.6% on FI's decision.
Mild negative on a thin name: Norcros flagged softer UK demand after both previews were written, a restructuring charge is likely, and the bar is disputed upward (ABG 88 vs SB1 80).

Lean down: Handelsbanken and Nordea both missed NII on funding costs, while Swedbank's 15 Oct consensus still asks for +4.1% q/q NII; a negative tail from the first capital statement since FI's IRB decision.

Lean up: the Delaware Supreme Court ruling, favourable and never released, the controlling owner's SEK 390m buying just before the closed period, and Virbac's strong companion-animal quarter outweigh a segment build ~0.5-1pp below consensus organic growth.

Slight negative: TTF gas at 59-85 against ~45 in Q2 raises the risk of a second guide trim after July's low-end steer, partly offset by the first FX tailwind and short-cover asymmetry; no register, so no positioning anchor.
